question: In reproductive health, what does the abbreviation mCPR stand for?
explanation: Think of mCPR as a handy way to track how many women of childbearing age are currently using modern family planning methods. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h1)

question: Which family planning method do most people in Nigeria tend to choose first?
explanation: In everyday practice, short-term options like injectables and male condoms are the most popular choices among clients. Great to know for your community postings! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h1)

question: Why do cities usually record higher family planning use than rural villages?

options.A: Better access to equipped health facilities and higher literacy
options.B: Rural health workers refuse to distribute any commodities
options.C: Contraceptives are strictly forbidden by law in villages
options.D: Traditional beliefs are completely absent in big cities

explanation: Being close to clinics and having better access to health education makes it much easier for city residents to get and use family planning services. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h2)

question: Which part of Nigeria generally records lower modern contraceptive prevalence rates?
explanation: National health surveys consistently show differences in mCPR across regions, with the northern zones generally recording lower rates than the southern zones. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h2)

question: What is a common cultural view in some Nigerian communities that affects family planning?

options.A: Children born in large numbers are automatically given free education
options.B: Large family sizes are seen as a sign of wealth and prestige
options.C: Small families are forbidden by ancestral spirits
options.D: Contraception is required by traditional law for all couples

explanation: In many cultures, having many children is traditionally viewed as a great blessing and a symbol of high status, which can make people hesitant about birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a common community myth about modern contraceptives?

options.A: They improve eyesight and physical endurance
options.B: They are foreign agents meant to reduce population
options.C: They cause permanent sterility in young women
options.D: They lead to severe congenital birth defects

explanation: Myths usually scare people by claiming contraceptives cause harm like infertility or birth defects—nobody spreads myths about them improving your eyesight! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h3)

question: Which international bodies often partner to support Nigeria's family planning supplies?
explanation: Organizations like UNFPA (United Nations Population Fund) and USAID play a massive role in funding and shipping family planning commodities to Nigeria. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h4)

question: What is a major focus of donor-supported family planning programs in primary health clinics?

options.A: Mandating contraceptive use for all married couples
options.B: Building private hospitals in every rural community
options.C: Replacing all local doctors with foreign medical experts
options.D: Preventing commodity stock-outs and training health staff

explanation: These programs focus heavily on making sure clinics never run out of supplies and helping local healthcare workers build their clinical skills. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h4)

question: A young, unmarried woman leaves a clinic without birth control because the nurse scolds her. What is this barrier called?
explanation: When personal judgments or scolding from healthcare staff stop a client from getting care, that is provider bias. As future nurses, we always want to keep our clinics welcoming and judgment-free! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h5)

question: A client asks for an injectable contraceptive at a clinic, but the shelf is empty due to delayed shipments. What is this called?
explanation: When a clinic runs completely out of supplies due to delivery delays, it's called a stock-out. It's a frustrating supply chain challenge, but easy to spot! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h5)

question: How can a clinic nurse best support a teenage girl looking for reproductive health advice?

options.A: Publicly reprimand her to discourage other teenagers
options.B: Report her immediately to local religious authorities
options.C: Provide confidential, non-judgmental counseling in a private space
options.D: Refuse service until her parents come to sign a consent form

explanation: Youth-friendly care is all about trust, privacy, and a warm attitude. Making teens feel safe encourages them to seek proper health guidance. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h6)

question: What is a major public health win when family planning services improve across Nigeria?

options.A: Reducing maternal and infant mortality rates
options.B: Guaranteed economic wealth for every household
options.C: Eliminating all infectious diseases in children
options.D: Removing the need for primary health care clinics

explanation: Proper birth spacing gives mothers and babies a fighting chance at better health, directly lowering maternal and infant deaths. Beautiful impact of nursing care! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h6)
